lead.headline: Oil Stays Above $114 While Attacks and Talks Go On in the Gulf
lead.deck: Saudi Arabia says it stopped more drones as three countries meet Iran's leaders.
body: Oil is the raw material for petrol and diesel, so its price ends up on the signs at filling stations. On Monday a barrel of Brent crude, the price many countries follow, closed at $115.81. Early on Tuesday it was $114.68.

Part of the reason is a fight in the Gulf region. The Houthis, an armed group in Yemen, keep attacking Saudi Arabia, which sells a great deal of oil. Saudi Arabia's allies said they destroyed three drones aimed at the capital, Riyadh, and southern areas on Monday.

There is also some diplomacy. On Monday, senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan met Iran's leaders in Tehran, and Iranian state media said they agreed to keep talking. Buyers are watching the Gulf closely.

world.headline: Europe's Living-Cost Anger Reaches Streets in Three Countries
world.deck: Higher fuel and energy bills are behind protests from France to Portugal.
body: Prices for fuel and energy have climbed across Europe, and last weekend people took to the streets. In France, the unrest led to 2,400 arrests, and President Emmanuel Macron said the protesters' demands were legitimate while condemning violence and looting.

The protests were not only in France. In Milan, in Italy, police clashed with protesters angry about public services and rising living costs. In Portugal, thousands marched against high housing costs.

The European Commission estimates the Iran conflict has cost Europe about 100 billion euros through disrupted trade and energy markets. It also says gas prices have jumped about 140% and diesel prices have doubled.
Fuel is part of the cost of moving almost everything by road, so a rise at the pump can show up in other prices too.

us.headline: More Than 30 Million Americans Have Already Voted
us.deck: A week before the midterms, early voting is running strongly.
body: The United States holds midterm elections on 3 November, halfway through a president's term, to choose members of Congress. Many people do not wait for that day. They vote early, by post or in person.
With a week to go, more than 30 million Americans have already voted, according to election trackers. In Louisiana, early voting ends on Tuesday, and more than 363,000 people have cast ballots there.
Early totals show how many people are taking part. They do not show who is winning, so the real result will come after election day.
us.why: Voting is how families have a say, and early voting gives people more than one chance to use it.

india.headline: Families on India's East Coast Move to Shelters Before Arnab
india.deck: A very severe cyclone is due to arrive in the small hours of Wednesday.
body: Imagine being told to leave your home before a storm. For more than 114,000 people in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, on India's east coast, that happened on Tuesday. They were moved from low-lying coastal districts to shelters.

The storm is Cyclone Arnab, a very severe cyclonic storm over the Bay of Bengal. India's weather office expects it to cross the coast between 2 am and 4 am on Wednesday, near Visakhapatnam. Gusts could reach 150 kilometres an hour.

Life on the coast has changed for a few days. Odisha closed schools in 16 of its 30 districts, and at least 50 trains and 21 flights were cancelled. In Andhra Pradesh, 1,351 pregnant women were taken to hospitals as a precaution. Andhra Pradesh also set up 1,087 medical teams and 1,274 ambulances.

lines.text: Good morning, and welcome to The Breakfast Table for Wednesday, 28 October. I'm Maya, with Sam. Today, how can news far away reach a family’s fuel bill? Let's follow the connection.
Our first story is about oil. We hear about its price in the news, but what does a barrel of oil have to do with a trip to the filling station?

Oil is the raw material for petrol and diesel. That is the connection. The price of crude oil can affect the fuel families buy. On Monday, Brent crude closed at $115.81 a barrel. Brent is an oil price many countries follow.

And the paper connects the price to fighting in the Gulf region. Saudi Arabia sells a great deal of oil. It has faced more attacks by the Houthis, an armed group in Yemen. But there are talks happening too?

Yes. Officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan met Iran's leaders in Tehran on Monday. Iranian state media said they agreed to keep talking. So buyers are watching both the attacks and the diplomacy. Dearer oil can mean dearer fuel, which is part of the cost of moving food and families around.

That helps explain our next story: living costs in Europe. Higher fuel and energy bills have brought people onto the streets. The paper reports protests in France, Italy and Portugal, with different concerns in each place.

In France, the unrest led to 2,400 arrests. President Emmanuel Macron said the protesters' demands were legitimate, while condemning violence and looting. In Milan, people were angry about public services and rising living costs. In Portugal, thousands marched against high housing costs.
So the connection with our oil story is fuel. The paper says fuel is part of the cost of moving almost everything by road. A higher price at the pump can therefore show up in other prices too.

Exactly. A fuel bill and a housing bill are different costs, but both matter to families. This is why the paper looks beyond the oil price itself. It helps us understand what people are concerned about in everyday life.
Now to the United States, where many people have already voted ahead of the midterm elections. Does a big early voting total tell us who is winning?

No. That is the important distinction. The elections take place on 3 November, halfway through a president's term, to choose members of Congress. People can vote early by post or in person, rather than waiting for election day.

More than 30 million Americans had already voted, according to the election trackers cited in the paper. That tells us about participation: how many people have taken part. It does not tell us the result.

Right. Early voting gives people more than one chance to vote. But we still have to wait for the result after election day. Keep that difference in mind: a count of people taking part is not a count showing who has won. Ready for a quick quiz?
Where did officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan meet Iran's leaders?
Tehran They met Iran's leaders in Tehran on Monday.
When do the US midterm elections take place?
3 November The paper says the midterms are on 3 November.
If petrol costs more, what else might cost more too, and why?
That is your question to talk about together. Thanks for joining us. Keep noticing the connections around you, and have a lovely day.
